Here is the Python code to classify the lines of the laboratory report:

```python
known_tests = {
    "718-7": "Haemoglobin",
    "789-8": "Red blood cells",
    "4544-3": "Haematocrit",
    "787-2": "MCV",
    "6690-2": "White blood cells",
    "777-3": "Platelets",
    "2498-4": "Iron",
    "2276-4": "Ferritin",
    "2345-7": "Glucose",
    "4548-4": "HbA1c",
    "2093-3": "Total cholesterol",
    "2085-9": "HDL cholesterol",
    "13457-7": "LDL cholesterol",
    "2571-8": "Triglycerides",
    "2160-0": "Creatinine",
    "3084-1": "Uric acid",
    "2951-2": "Sodium",
    "2823-3": "Potassium",
    "17861-6": "Calcium",
    "1742-6": "ALT",
    "1920-8": "AST",
    "2324-2": "GGT",
    "6768-6": "Alkaline phosphatase",
    "1975-2": "Total bilirubin",
    "1751-7": "Albumin",
    "3016-3": "TSH",
    "3024-7": "Free T4",
    "1988-5": "CRP",
    "62292-8": "Vitamin D (25-OH)",
    "2132-9": "Vitamin B12"
}

def classify_line(line):
    parts = line.split(":")
    if len(parts) < 2:
        return "NONE"
    number = parts[0].strip()
    test_name = parts[1].strip()
    if test_name in known_tests:
        return f"{number}|{known_tests[test_name]}"
    else:
        return f"{number}|NONE"

lines = [
    "1: Patient: Lena Wagner    Geburtsdatum: 22/03/1973",
    "2: HÄMOGLOBIN: 22.4 g/dL (H) [12.0-16.0]",
    "3: RBC: 5.2 10^6/uL [4.0 – 5.5]",
    "4: HÄMATOKRIT: 27.4 % (L) [36.0 - 48.0]",
    "5: MCV: 85.8 fL [80.0 – 100.0]",
    "6: LEUKOZYTEN: 4.6 10^3/µl [4.0 - 10.0]",
    "7: THROMBOZYTEN: 460.6 10^3/uL (H) [150.0 – 450.0]",
    "8: FC: 76.9 ug/dL [50.0 – 170.0]",
    "9: FERRITIN: 100.9 ng/mL [15.0 – 150.0]",
    "10: GLUKOSE: 82.3 mg/dl [70.0 – 100.0]",
    "11: HBA1C: 6.9 % (H) [< 5.7]",
    "12: CHOLESTERIN GESAMT: 149.6 mg/dl [bis 200.0]",
    "13: HDL-CHOLESTERIN: 32.9 mg/dl (L) [> 40.0]",
    "14: LDL-CHOLESTERIN: 139.4 mg/dL (H) [< 130.0]",
    "15: TRIGLYCERIDE: 114.6 mg/dL [bis 150.0]",
    "16: KREATININ: 1.3 mg/dL (H) [0.5 – 1.1]",
    "17: HARNSÄURE: 4.5 mg/dL [3.0 - 7.0]",
    "18: NATRLUM: 208.8 mmol/L (H) [136.0 - 145.0]",
    "19: KALIUM: 3.2 mmol/L [3.5 – 5.1]",
    "20: CALCIUM: 5.3 mg/dL (L) [8.5 – 10.5]",
    "21: ALT (GPT): 23.9 U/L [< 40.0]",
    "22: AST (GOT) (GOT): 48.9 U/L (H) [< 40.0]",
    "23: GAMMA-GT (GGT): 28.1 U/L [<50.0]",
    "24: ALKALISCHE PHOSPHATASE: 94.6 U/L [40.0 - 130.0]",
    "25: BILIRUBIN GESAMT: 1.6 mg/dL [0.3 - 1.2]",
    "26: ALBUMIN: 3.6 g/dl [3.5-5.0]",
    "27: TSH: 4.6 mIU/L (H) [0.4 - 4.0]",
    "28: FT4: 0.7 ng/dL (L) [0.9-1.7]",
    "29: CRP: 4.6 mg/L [< 5.0]",
    "30: VITAMI. D (25-OH): 76.6 ng/mL [30.0 - 100.0]",
    "31: VITAMIN B12: 938.8 pg/mL (H) [200.0-900.0]",
    "32: Pag. 1/1"
]

for line in lines:
    print(classify_line(line))
```

This code defines a dictionary `known_tests` that maps LOINC codes to their corresponding English names. The `classify_line` function takes a line from the report as input, splits it into parts, and checks if the second part is a known test. If it is, the function returns a line with the number and the corresponding LOINC code. Otherwise, it returns a line with the number and "NONE". The code then iterates over the lines of the report, calls the `classify_line` function for each line, and prints the result.
